fact: WHO states that Congo adopted a national strategic plan for the national health information system (SNIS) and e-health for 2020-2024 in November 2019, that its implementation is insufficient, and that there is no legislative or functional multisectoral framework coordinating the health information system.

WHO states that DHIS2 has been used since 2020 as the national warehouse 'at the peripheral level' for routine health data, enabling electronic aggregation, with data completeness of 87% and timeliness of 47.9% in 2024; the document does not say whether entry is at the facility or the district office.

The health ministry's PNDS states that Congo drew up a national strategic plan for the SNIS and e-health 2020-2024 in November 2019, and that execution of its 2020-2024 action plan was halted in early 2020 by the Covid-19 response.

The PNDS 2023-2026 itself names DHIS2 as the principal platform adopted for collecting and processing health information and sets revising the digital strategy to align with the PNDS as the main digitalisation task; no date is given for the statement, so the document's published date is used.

The PNDS lists a directorate of health information, evaluation and research within the health ministry and a database manager in every health district among the SNIS's strengths, with district returns going to that directorate; undated, so the published date is used.

The PNDS states that the DHIS2 platform was built with Global Fund and Gavi support to manage the whole national health information system, and lists insufficient financial resources for data management among the SNIS's weaknesses; undated, so the published date is used.

The PNDS states that data are produced on paper as compiled reports in nearly all public, private and faith-based facilities and sent to the health districts for entry, all 12 departments and 52 districts being trained on DHIS2 and given a modem and three years of internet; facility completeness is above 87% and timeliness 48.94%; undated, so the published date is used.

The PNDS states that standard collection tools exist in health centres (CSI), district referral hospitals (HRD) and private facilities but not general hospitals, whose forms are configured in DHIS2 with monthly reporting from hospitals still to begin; health posts are not mentioned; undated, so the published date is used.

The PNDS states that facilities produce their reports on paper and the health districts key them into DHIS2, and that paper collection tools remain much used while the computer tools provided are not often used; no count of facilities entering their own data is given; undated, so the published date is used.

The health ministry's national health policy states that the health information system is organised over the three levels of the pyramid but does not work effectively: the information exists in health facilities, but the system cannot yet collect and transcribe it through a computerised system, only some programmes and projects doing so in a targeted, siloed way.
